title: Number of Senior Citizens
summary: Given an array of passenger details, count how many passengers are over 60 years old by examining the age field in the third and fourth characters of each detail string.
statement: Given an array of passenger details, count how many passengers are over 60 years old by examining the age field in the third and fourth characters of each detail string.
constraints: Each fixed-length detail string stores a ten-digit phone number, one gender character, a two-digit age, and a two-digit seat number.
The age occupies zero-based positions eleven and twelve.
Return the number of passengers strictly older than sixty.
reference_solution:
def count_senior_passengers(details):
    return sum(int(detail[11:13])>60 for detail in details)
hints: Use the fixed field positions rather than parsing the other fields.
Slice characters eleven through twelve inclusive.
Convert the two digits to an integer and count values greater than sixty.
Every record has the same layout, so the slice isolates exactly its age and the strict comparison matches the definition.
editorial: Every record has the same layout, so the slice isolates exactly its age and the strict comparison matches the definition.

tests.explanation: The first two ages are 75 and 92, so two passengers are over sixty.
Ages twenty and fifty-six produce zero senior passengers.
